requirement:
For the records displayed by {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`,
`habeas mdbook` MUST generate a detail subchapter under the index chapter for
each recorded nextest test process, identifying its binary, test name, attempt,
test-attempt outcome, and originating run. Each report MUST show its instrumented
first-party Rust source lines and execution counts, distinguishing executed
from unexecuted lines, using the source captured for that run, and link back to
the index.
Coverage from associated child processes MUST remain distinguishable from
coverage recorded by the nextest test process itself.
rationale: I found no gaps. Every obligation has code reachable from an {impl} item and a test that asserts its outcome. **Obligations, code and tests** 1. **A detail subchapter under the index for each recorded test process.** - Code: `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#fn[populate_in]` builds a `Record` for every attempt on disk. It builds a `Chapter` with `detail(record, &index_path)` for each record and appends it to the index chapter's `sub_items`. `populate_in` is reached from `fn[populate]`, which carries the {impl}. Every record shown in the summary's provenance table has a link and a chapter. - Tests: `reports_identify_attempts_and_union_child_counts_without_discarding_profiles` asserts four sub-items (two attempts plus their source chapters). It also asserts that each summary link matches a detail chapter. 2. **Each report identifies binary, test name, attempt, outcome and originating run.** - Code: `fn[detail]` prints a heading with the test name. Its "Run and attempt details" block prints Binary, Test, Attempt and Outcome, plus Run id, run outcome and capture time. - Tests: `reports_identify_attempts_and_union_child_counts_without_discarding_profiles` asserts `Binary: binary`, `Attempt: 1`, `Outcome: success`, `Test: one` and `Run: {first_run}`. 3. **Instrumented first-party Rust source lines and execution counts, executed versus unexecuted, using the source captured for that run.** - Code: `fn[detail]` emits JSON with per-process `lines`. Counts are u64 values serialized as strings. It also emits a `habeasRenderCoverage` call and a link to the run's source page. `fn[source_page]` publishes the run's `run.sources` and posts them to the parent frame. `assets/coverage-viewer.js` renders each line with its count and labels it "executed" or "unexecuted". It takes source text from the posted sources and accepts them only if they come from the iframe and carry the matching run id. - Tests: - `.github/scripts/coverage-viewer.test.mjs` checks that the 18446744073709551615 count is preserved and that "executed" and "unexecuted" are shown. It checks the captured source text, rejection of messages from an unrelated window or a different run, and lazy per-file rendering. - `reports_identify_attempts_and_union_child_counts_without_discarding_profiles` rewrites `code.rs` and asserts that the saved source and counts persist. - `rendered_detail_scripts_remain_literal_across_blank_lines` renders the chapter through pulldown_cmark and checks the embedded script and JSON data. - `filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source` checks that the captured source is still shown after the on-disk source changes. 4. **Link back to the index.** - Code: `fn[detail]` and `fn[source_page]` both emit `[Back to coverage index](...)`. - Test: `reports_identify_attempts_and_union_child_counts_without_discarding_profiles` asserts `[Back to coverage index](../coverage.html)` in each detail chapter. 5. **Child-process coverage stays distinguishable from the test process's own coverage.** - Code: `fn[detail]` sets `kind` to "Test" when `process.pid == attempt.pid` and "Child" otherwise. The JS viewer renders a separate "Child process N" section for each process. - Tests: the Rust test asserts `"kind":"Test"`, `"kind":"Child"` and the child's counts. The JS test asserts `Child process 2` and that the child's lines and source are kept separate. **Other checks** - The unreadable-coverage path of `detail` is tested in `maps_distinguish_no_runs_zero_hits_stale_and_incomplete_coverage`. - The helpers `file_map`, `union`, `readable` and `escaped` are reached from the {impl} items, so they need no references of their own. - I found no unspecified behavior outside what the subject or the other requirements the same code marks with {impl} describe.

text: :::{req} index.details
For the records displayed by {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`,
`habeas mdbook` MUST generate a detail subchapter under the index chapter for
each recorded nextest test process, identifying its binary, test name, attempt,
test-attempt outcome, and originating run. Each report MUST show its instrumented
first-party Rust source lines and execution counts, distinguishing executed
from unexecuted lines, using the source captured for that run, and link back to
the index.
Coverage from associated child processes MUST remain distinguishable from
coverage recorded by the nextest test process itself.
:::{req} index.summary
The coverage index MUST display the combined view selected under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. It MUST identify the
contributing runs and show each selected test's binary, test name, attempt,
capture time, command, selection, and outcome, including missing or stale
coverage. It MUST show source revisions and uncommitted-source state when
available rather than present records from several runs as one run.
For first-party Rust files under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, the summary MUST compute
line coverage from the union of instrumented file-and-line locations in the
selected fresh records, including their associated child-process records.
Each location MUST count once in the denominator and count as covered when any
selected record has a positive execution count for it. Percentages MUST be
computed from those union counts rather than averaged across process reports.
A view with no instrumented lines MUST show coverage as unavailable. The index
MUST link to {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.details`, visibly identify
incomplete coverage, and MUST NOT imply that every current test has coverage
merely because all available records are valid.
